title: google-labs-code/stitch-skills — A library of Agent Skills designed to work with the Stitch MCP server. Each skill follows the Agent Skills open standard, for compatibility with coding agents such as Antigravity, Gemini CLI, Claude Code, Cursor.
content:
A collection of agent skills and plugins for Google Stitch, following the Agent Skills open standard. Compatible with coding agents such as Codex, Antigravity, Gemini CLI, Claude Code, Cursor, and OpenCode (manual install).
The fastest way to set up the full Stitch plugin suite globally.
Add the Stitch Skills marketplace, then install the plugins you need.
Via CLI (recommended)
codex plugin marketplace add google-labs-code/stitch-skills --ref main \
  --sparse .agents/plugins \
  --sparse plugins/stitch-design \
  --sparse plugins/stitch-build \
  --sparse plugins/stitch-utilities
[!TIP]
The --sparse flags are optional — they limit the checkout to only the
listed paths for a faster clone. Omit them to pull the entire repository.
Via the Codex UI
Navigate to Settings → Plugin Marketplaces → Add and fill in:
Once the marketplace is registered, install any combination of:
- stitch-design — design-focused skills
- stitch-build — build and component skills
- stitch-utilities — utility and helper skills
# Claude Code — installs into the current project
npx plugins add google-labs-code/stitch-skills --scope project --target claude-code# Cursor — installs into the current workspace
npx plugins add google-labs-code/stitch-skills --scope workspace --target cursor
OpenCode does not use npx plugins / npx skills or the Codex/Claude marketplace layout.
Install skills and the Stitch MCP server manually:
1. Skills — copy the skill folders you need into a discoverable path:
# Project-local (recommended)
mkdir -p .opencode/skills
cp -R plugins/stitch-design/skills/generate-design .opencode/skills/generate-design
# repeat for other skills under plugins/*/skills/
OpenCode also discovers .claude/skills/ and .agents/skills/ (see OpenCode skills docs).
Naming: OpenCode requires skill name frontmatter to be lowercase kebab-case and match the directory name. Skills that use stitch::… names (or other non-kebab forms) need the name field and folder renamed before OpenCode will load them. Extra frontmatter such as allowed-tools is ignored.
2. Stitch MCP — add a remote MCP entry in project opencode.json or ~/.config/opencode/opencode.json after completing the Stitch MCP setup:
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "mcp": {
    "stitch": {
      "type": "remote",
      "url": "YOUR_STITCH_MCP_URL",
      "enabled": true
    }
  }
}
Replace YOUR_STITCH_MCP_URL with the endpoint from the Stitch MCP setup flow (credentials/env vars from that guide still apply).
Tool names inside skill instructions may differ from OpenCode builtins (webfetch / bash instead of web_fetch / run_command). Prefer the OpenCode tool names when adapting a skill for OpenCode.
Choose only the specific skills you need.
Important
Stitch Design Skills often have inter-dependencies. If you choose to install skills selectively, ensure you include all required dependencies.
npx skills add google-labs-code/stitch-skills
You can run the following commands to see the help documentation for plugins and skills:
npx plugins --help
npx skills --help
These skills require the Stitch MCP server to be configured and running in your agent's environment. Make sure you have followed the Stitch MCP Setup Instructions to register the server and set up appropriate environment variables and credentials.
Docs navigation: If a link on stitch.withgoogle.com/docs redirects incorrectly, open the target path under the same host (e.g. https://stitch.withgoogle.com/docs/learn/device-types/).
Core design workflows for creating, managing, and optimizing designs within Stitch.
Code generation, framework integration, and asset compilation from Stitch designs.
Supporting tools for enhancing prompts, generating design specs, and enforcing design standards.
plugins/
├── stitch-design/          — Core design workflow plugin
│   ├── plugin.json
│   └── skills/
│       ├── code-to-design/
│       ├── generate-design/
│       ├── manage-design-system/
│       ├── extract-design-md/
│       ├── extract-static-html/
│       └── upload-to-stitch/
├── stitch-build/           — Code generation & build plugin
│   ├── plugin.json
│   └── skills/
│       ├── react-components/    — stitch::react-components
│       ├── react-native/
│       ├── react-vite-dashboard/
│       ├── remotion/
│       └── shadcn-ui/
└── stitch-utilities/       — Design utilities & assistants plugin
    ├── plugin.json
    └── skills/
        ├── design-md/
        ├── enhance-prompt/
        ├── site-md/
        ├── stitch-loop/
        └── taste-design/
Each skill follows the Agent Skills standard:
skills/<skill-name>/
├── SKILL.md           — The "Mission Control" for the agent
├── scripts/           — Executable enforcers (Validation & Networking)
├── resources/         — The knowledge base (Checklists & Style Guides)
└── examples/          — The "Gold Standard" syntactically valid references
All new skills need to follow the file structure above to implement the Agent Skills open standard.
- Validation: Skills that convert Stitch HTML to other UI frameworks and validate the syntax.
- Decoupling Data: Skills that convert static design content into external mock data files.
- Generate Designs: Skills that generate new design screens in Stitch from a given set of data.
This is not an officially supported Google product. This project is not eligible for the Google Open Source Software Vulnerability Rewards Program.

report.summary: Google Labs released stitch-skills, an open-standard library of Agent Skills that lets coding agents like Claude Code, Cursor, and Gemini CLI drive Google Stitch design workflows via MCP.
report.background: Google Stitch, launched from Google Labs at I/O 2025, turns text or image prompts into UI designs and front-end code. Separately, Anthropic's Agent Skills format (a folder with a SKILL.md instruction file plus scripts, resources and examples) emerged as a de facto packaging standard for agent capabilities, and MCP became the common protocol for connecting models to tools. Stitch-skills sits at the intersection: it packages Stitch design operations as portable skills and assumes a Stitch MCP server is running. The repo also reflects a broader shift away from vendor-locked agent features toward reusable, cross-agent artifacts — the same skill folder is meant to run in Codex, Gemini CLI, Claude Code, Cursor, Antigravity and OpenCode. Notably, Google labels it a Labs experiment, not an officially supported product, signalling that the interfaces and skill names may still change.
key_points: Three plugin bundles: stitch-design covers creating, managing and optimizing designs (generate-design, code-to-design, manage-design-system, extract-design-md, upload-to-stitch); stitch-build turns designs into code (React, React Native, Vite dashboards, Remotion, shadcn-ui); stitch-utilities adds prompt enhancement, design specs and design-standard enforcement.

Installation is a one-liner per agent: a Codex plugin marketplace add command with optional sparse checkout flags, npx plugins add for Claude Code and Cursor, or manual copying of skill folders into .opencode/skills for OpenCode — which also requires renaming skills to lowercase kebab-case.

A Stitch MCP server is mandatory. Skills only describe the workflow; the actual design operations run through a remote MCP endpoint configured in the agent's environment with credentials and environment variables from the Stitch setup guide.

Skills are interdependent. Google explicitly warns that selectively installing design skills without their dependencies will break workflows, and each skill folder must follow the standard layout: SKILL.md, scripts for validation, resources as a knowledge base, and examples as reference implementations.

The repo includes a recurring pipeline pattern: convert Stitch HTML into other UI frameworks with syntax validation, extract static design content into external mock data files, then regenerate new screens from that data — essentially a design-to-code loop.
report.impact: For the AI industry, this is a notable endorsement of cross-vendor standards: Google shipping skills designed to run inside Anthropic's Claude Code and Cursor, rather than only its own Gemini CLI, suggests agent capability packaging is consolidating around SKILL.md plus MCP instead of proprietary plugin formats. For developers, it lowers the barrier to wiring AI-generated UI into real React or React Native codebases, but adds operational overhead — MCP server setup, dependency management, and tool-name mismatches between agents (webfetch versus web_fetch) that require manual adaptation. For regular users, the practical effect is indirect: faster, more consistent design-to-prototype turnaround inside tools they already use, with more design artefacts (specs, mock data, component libraries) arriving automatically. The main caveat is maturity — an unsupported Labs project with unstable interfaces, no security-bounty coverage, and a manual-install path for OpenCode users.
report.tools: Watch the repo itself (google-labs-code/stitch-skills) for skill updates, plus Google Stitch and its MCP setup docs for the server endpoint. Related items worth trying: Anthropic's Agent Skills specification and reference skills, the MCP specification and inspector for debugging your Stitch connection, and npx plugins / npx skills for installing skill bundles across Codex, Claude Code and Cursor. For the build side, the bundled React, shadcn-ui, Remotion and React Native skills double as templates for writing your own agent skills.
